newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds end higher unaffected by bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds end higher unaffected by bomb attack.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Wednesday and traders said trading was unaffected by a bomb attack in Jerusalem because the buy orders were issued before the event.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.05 pct to 110.45
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.1 pct to 110.56
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.04 pct 109.99
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.3 pct to 110.59
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 108.23
Volume including Makams was an average 169 million shekels.

"It is difficult to see what effect the bombs will have on the bond market. The buy orders were given this morning, before the bombs went off. So if there is any influence we will see it tomorrow," said Baruch Glicksberg, investment manager for a major institutional investor.
Tel Aviv shares fell on Wednesday, reversing morning gains, after two bombs ripped through an outdoor market in Jewish west Jerusalem, killing 13 people.

"It is very bad that such a thing has happened both for the stock and bond market," Glicksberg said. "Recently both markets have been extremely optimistic, turning all news into good news. So it is difficult to foresee how the markets will react in the coming days."
Prices of CPI-linked bonds were higher on Wednesday while those of unlinked bonds were stable, Glicksberg said.

"Demand is up on CPI-linked bonds because redemptions are higher than new issues. The government is issuing less bonds because it has just cut the budget and because it is raising money through the privatisation process," Glicksberg said.
The Israeli cabinet approved an 800 million shekel cut in the 1997 budget last week.

The cuts were the third round of budget slashing since the draft 1997 budget was presented last autumn. The government had earlier approved some seven billion shekels in cuts and revenue- raising measures.

Prices of unlinked bonds were stable because of fears of a high July consumer price index and a hike in interest rates in the coming months. "July's CPI is expected to be a high 0.9 percent and interest rates are not expected to fall," said a trader.
July's CPI will be published on August 15.
The Bank of Israel said on Monday it was leaving unchanged at 12.7 percent its key lending rate for August. The central bank slashed its base lending rate in mid-June by 1.2 percentage points.

The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices. The shekel has recovered some of its losses against the dollar in the past two weeks.
Prices of dollar-linked bonds fell on the strengthening of the shekel against the dollar on Tuesday, the trader said.
The shekel declined against the dollar on Wednesday. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5460 shekels compared with 3.5340 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.55 shekels)
